chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn 'Uqba from Zayd al-Shahham said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the reward for one who visits one of you?' He said, '(It is) like the one who visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the theological equivalence between visiting the Imams and visiting the Prophet, underscoring their role as the living continuation of prophetic guidance. This comparison elevates Ziyarah from a mere social visit to a profound act of worship that reinforces the bond between the believer and the divine authority (Wilayah). It reflects the Shia belief that the Imams are the perfect exemplars of the Prophet’s Sunnah, making their presence a means of drawing closer to Allah.
